speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin my assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and is the pain sharp or dull?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malignant Esophageal Perforation (Boerhaave Syndrome)

Given the history of forceful retching after alcohol consumption followed by sudden onset of chest pain and respiratory distress in a 51-year-old male, this clinical presentation is highly suggestive of a spontaneous esophageal rupture. I am requesting an emergent CT scan of the chest with oral contrast to confirm the diagnosis.
